text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Cyprus says no to the U.S. proposal to ban military overflights, but that it will take unilateral measures to reduce tension if necessary.
- U.N. envoy to Cyprus Gustave Feissel says Turkish threats to knock out the S-300 missile system are unacceptable.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Missile row hits bookings by British holidaymakers, says tourism official.
- Cyprus rebuffs the U.S. on the flight moratorium.
- Cyprus stock exchange falls to an all-time low.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Dollar roars higher against the Cyprus pound.
- Laiki (Popular Bank) lead in its credit card services.
- T-bill auction today will be watched for signs to see if the Central Bank's efforts to lower interest rates are moving in the right direction.
HARAVGHI
- Crime gang in Nicosia seeks permission to operate a "protection and insurance service".
- The presidential palace considers a cabinet reshuffle.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Disy and Diko parties' partnership in government hangs in the balance. Disy is expected to make goodwill gesture to Diko today.
- Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan promises to send Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash water and students.
SIMERINI
- Diko party leader Spyros Kyprianou demands the resignation of Justice Minister Alecos Evangelou.
- The U.S. will raise the issue of banning military overflights again.
